title: E6 task-decoding checkpoint form A
instructions: Read this original practice prompt and make all three task-decoding decisions before submitting. Prompt: The Student Skills Newsletter asks for an article for secondary-school readers. Write about one habit you learned during a school group project. Explain how you have used it, or could use it, to solve a problem outside school. Support your explanation with one specific actual or realistic example.

parts.prompt: Which task contract preserves the topic, command, audience, scope and personal application?

options.text: I will tell teachers why every group project should receive a grade.
I will explain to secondary-school readers how one group-project habit can solve an outside-school problem, using one actual or realistic example.
I will list several school habits and describe my favourite classmates.
I will argue that problems outside school are more difficult than schoolwork.

choice_rationales.A: The prompt does not ask for a grading policy or address teachers.
choice_rationales.B: This keeps the named audience, one-habit scope, explanatory command, transfer and specific example.
choice_rationales.C: Several habits break the one-focus limit, and classmate description does not explain transfer.
choice_rationales.D: The prompt asks for explanation of one application, not a comparison of difficulty.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The correct task contract names one learned habit, one outside-school application, one example and the stated readers.

parts.prompt: Which THREE elements are explicit requirements of the prompt?

options.text: One habit learned during a school group project
A comparison of at least three group projects
An outside-school problem to which the habit applies
One specific actual or realistic example
Proof that the solution succeeded perfectly

choice_rationales.A: The topic and one-focus limit require one learned habit.
choice_rationales.B: No comparison or minimum of three projects appears.
choice_rationales.C: The command requires transfer beyond school.
choice_rationales.D: The final sentence explicitly requires a specific example.
choice_rationales.E: A realistic future use is allowed, so perfect past success is not required.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The response must focus on one project habit, connect it to an outside-school problem and develop one specific example.

parts.prompt: Which proposed response is most clearly off-task?

options.text: Explain how assigning roles during a science project could help organise a neighbourhood clean-up.
Explain how checking progress during a presentation project helped coordinate a family move.
Narrate every event in a school project without identifying a habit or showing any use outside school.
Explain how listening before deciding in a group task could help resolve a disagreement in a sports club.

choice_rationales.A: This selects one habit and a realistic outside-school application.
choice_rationales.B: This supplies one actual transfer example.
choice_rationales.C: The narrative omits both the named habit and the required transfer beyond school.
choice_rationales.D: This preserves one habit, one problem and a realistic application.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A school-project narrative alone does not answer the explanatory transfer task.
